subject: Accelerated onramp checklist and canary cadence — SummitRidge
messages:
From: Michael Zhao <michael.zhao@summitridge.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: timeline and onramp scope

Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency and cost breakdowns were very helpful. Execs like the idea of an accelerated onramp if we can shorten the typical 12-week cadence. Our target internal go-live window is ~10 weeks from signature; can you send an example accelerated MAP that embeds the canary/migration/training milestones and a proposed measurement plan?

Key asks from our side:
- A compact checklist we can attach to procurement for sign-off
- Canary thresholds (error budget, latency p95, token cost)
- Training plan for 20 agents (2 sessions + recordings)
- Clear handoff owners and acceptance gates

I attached a short scope doc to orient you. Happy to take a quick call tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Michael
Director of Platform Ops
SummitRidge Analytics
[Attachment: summitridge_scope_initial.docx]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Michael Zhao <michael.zhao@summitridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: timeline and onramp scope

Michael — thanks for the clear asks and the scope doc.

We can support an accelerated onramp and have sketched a compact MAP that folds in a canary window, data migration checkpoints, and training for end users. I attached a working MAP (Accelerated_MAP_v0.1) and a short PDF with canary thresholds. High-level proposal below — happy to iterate during a 30-min MAP alignment call.

Proposed 8-week accelerated sequence (assumes signature + immediate kickoff):
1) Week 0 (Kickoff): mutual action plan, security questionnaire finalization, access provisioning
2) Week 1–2 (Prep & Migration): S3/KV export tests, schema validation, prefix caching plan
3) Week 3 (Canary Phase 1): 2% traffic; measure latency p95, 99, token cost, error budget
4) Week 4–5 (Observability & Scaling): adjust batching/quantization profiles, autoscale smoke tests
5) Week 6 (Canary Phase 2): 10% traffic; acceptance gates for rollout if thresholds met
6) Week 7 (Training Week): two live sessions + recordings for 20 agents; runbook handoff
7) Week 8 (Cutover): gradual ramp to 100% with rollback policy and SLA enablement

Canary thresholds (excerpt):
- Latency p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms
- Token cost within 15% of bench baseline
- Error budget < 0.5% for 72-hour sliding window

Immediate asks for your team: confirm target cutover week (we proposed week 8), and share a sample production traffic pattern (peak qps).

I’ll poll Ben for capacity availability and Jonas for rollout orchestration notes. If everyone’s aligned I’ll formalize the MAP and share a tracked spreadsheet we can attach to procurement.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: accelerated_map_v0.1.xlsx]

Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: accelerated MAP — owners and immediate blockers

Team — forwarding Michael’s asks and the draft map I just sent. We need to lock the following today so we can produce the procurement checklist by EOD tomorrow: 

Action items (owners):
- Infrastructure capacity confirmation (Ben) — confirm pool/priority for weeks 3 and 6 canary windows and a rollback node pool
- Rollout orchestration plan + canary automation (Jonas) — scripted traffic injection and automatic fallback policy, define alerting hooks
- Pricing acceptance gates & purchase checklist (Marissa) — compact procurement packet (SOW + MAP + acceptance criteria)
- Security items (me) — map outstanding questionnaire items and provide sample audit log export format

Notes:
- Training: we will run two 60-min sessions in Week 7; Marissa, can you create the agent curriculum?
- Attachments: reference accelerated_map_v0.1.xlsx and canary_thresholds.pdf when composing the procurement packet.

Ben — please reply with whether the dedicated pool is available on Week 3 and Week 6. Jonas — any concerns about automated rollback complexity given SummitRidge’s planned traffic pattern?

Thanks — I’ll consolidate responses and draft the procurement-ready sheet.

Irene

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: accelerated MAP — owners and immediate blockers

Quick update — we can reserve the dedicated pool for the two canary windows. Capacity notes:
- Week 3 (2% traffic): trivial from a GPU standpoint, will use a transient shard on our preemptible pool for 72 hours
- Week 6 (10% traffic): will require reserved nodes (I’ll allocate 4x A100 equivalent slots)

I’ll preload the KV cache snapshot during Week 1–2 migration tests and confirm performance delta by end of Week 2. No blockers on rollback — we’ll maintain a pinned model variant and a fast-switch routing policy.

Ben
Senior Infrastructure Eng
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: canary_thresholds.pdf]
